To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

cholesterol (Chol), a key lipid component of cell membranes, considerably impacts the binding affinity of CCR5 receptor to the HIV‐entry inhibitor maraviroc and that Chol decreases the structural flexibility of the receptor.
Chol has a considerable impact in the binding affinity and conformational dynamics of the chemokine C‐C motif receptor type 5 (CCR5).

Chol depletion increases the affinity of maraviro to CCR5, and that the mechanisms by which this happens seem to involve the stabilization of a distinct receptor‐conformations with restrained structural dynamics.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a novel and important role of Chol in CCR5 receptor function, and this may have significant implications on HIV infection and CCL5‐CCR5‐mediated inflammatory processes.
the role of the membrane environment in receptor‐ligand interaction.
the impact of Chol on receptor conformational dynamics, which in turn impacts ligand binding and signaling, a fundamental aspect of the G‐protein‐receptor family.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the presence of Chols in the receptor‐ligand complex is not required for the receptor‐ligands interaction, but Chols are required to modulate the receptor‐conformations, which is essential for the binding process.
Chol impacts on CCR5‐ligand binding affinity and receptor dynamics, but it does not affect the binding site of the CCR5 ligand.
the Chol environment is not permissive to the binding and/or activation of CCR5 by its ligands, including HIV gp120.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Chol is not an inhibitor of HIV infection as previously proposed, but rather an inhibitor of the CCR5‐ligand interaction.
Chol depletion in the membrane environment could increase the CCR5 signaling efficiency.
Chol depletion increases maraviroc binding to CCR5, which could be an important mechanism to be considered for HIV infection and drug resistance.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Chol is a modulator of C‐terminal helix flexibility and that the presence of Cholesterol decreases the affinity of maraviro to CCR5.
the Chol environment has a considerable impact in CCR5 receptor‐ligand binding, which is likely to be relevant for the understanding of the mechanism of CCR5 receptor activation.
Chol depletion is not a viable therapeutic strategy to block HIV infection, as previously hypothesized.
